> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

**Outcome:** No defects found in the tested scope; two optional notes (test coverage for the Mute/Unmute guards, and the combination with open PR #13405) are collapsed below.

<details><summary>Verified</summary>

- `mute` and `unmute` are explicit and idempotent and show the usual OSD. `raise`, `lower`, `+N`/`-N` and `mute-toggle` behave as they do on the base; only the usage line differs.
- Once the menu's guard check has run, exactly one of Mute/Unmute shows when the output is unmuted or muted, and neither shows when no sink resolves. When the default sink is a DSP sink, the guard reads the same sink that the action changes.

- The brightness rows pass `+5%` / `5%-`, the same arguments the brightness keys use. All five visible controls (Volume Up/Down, whichever of Mute/Unmute applies, Brightness Up/Down) are found from root search.
- The new test fails against the base script (`Unknown volume action: mute`). The branch merges cleanly onto current `quattro`, and the menu tests still pass after the merge.
</details>

# Optional test improvement: cover the Mute/Unmute `when:` guards

Status: test gap, not a defect. The guards at the reviewed head (6d7c9ab8) behave correctly; none of the repository's tests notices the mutations below.

## Demonstrated benefit (surviving mutations)

Two deliberate mutations of `default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc` at the reviewed head:

```diff
# M1: swap the guards between the rows
-  "trigger.mute": {..."when":"[[ $(pactl get-sink-mute \"$(omarchy-audio-output-sink)\") == *no ]]",...},
-  "trigger.unmute": {..."when":"[[ $(pactl get-sink-mute \"$(omarchy-audio-output-sink)\") == *yes ]]",...},
+  "trigger.mute": {..."when":"[[ $(pactl get-sink-mute \"$(omarchy-audio-output-sink)\") == *yes ]]",...},
+  "trigger.unmute": {..."when":"[[ $(pactl get-sink-mute \"$(omarchy-audio-output-sink)\") == *no ]]",...},

# M2: drop the Unmute guard (both rows show while unmuted)
-  "trigger.unmute": {...,"label":"Unmute","when":"[[ ... == *yes ]]","action":"omarchy-audio-output-volume unmute"},
+  "trigger.unmute": {...,"label":"Unmute","action":"omarchy-audio-output-volume unmute"},
```

Actual results with each mutant (stock tests unchanged):

| Tree | menu-test.sh | menu-guards-test.sh | audio-output-volume-test.sh |
|---|---|---|---|
| head | pass (127 ok) | pass (18 ok) | pass (4 ok) |
| M1 swapped guards | pass (127 ok) | pass (18 ok) | pass (4 ok) |
| M2 Unmute without `when` | pass (127 ok) | pass (18 ok) | pass (4 ok) |

## Suggested test (append to `test/shell.d/audio-output-volume-test.sh`)

It reuses the file's existing `pactl` and `omarchy-audio-output-sink` stubs and builds the guard batch for these two rows with the menu's own `MenuModel.guardScript`.

```bash

# The menu decides between Mute and Unmute from the same sink the action
# changes. Build the guard batch the shell runs for those two rows and ask it
# in each state: exactly one of them has to show.
require_command node
guard_script=$(node -e '
  const fs = require("fs")
  const path = require("path")
  const menu = require(path.join(process.env.ROOT, "shell/plugins/menu/MenuModel.js"))
  const items = menu.parseMenuJsonc(fs.readFileSync(path.join(process.env.ROOT, "default/omarchy/omarchy-menu.jsonc"), "utf8"))
  const rows = Object.fromEntries(items.filter(item => ["trigger.mute", "trigger.unmute"].includes(item.id)).map(item => [item.id, item]))
  process.stdout.write(menu.guardScript(rows))
')

# The batch snapshots installed packages first; keep that off the real pacman.
printf '#!/bin/bash\nexit 0\n' >"$stub_dir/pacman"
chmod +x "$stub_dir/pacman"

echo no >"$stub_dir/muted"
[[ $(bash -c "$guard_script") == $'trigger.mute:w:1\ntrigger.unmute:w:0' ]] || fail "menu offers Mute and not Unmute while the output is unmuted"
pass "menu offers Mute and not Unmute while the output is unmuted"

echo yes >"$stub_dir/muted"
[[ $(bash -c "$guard_script") == $'trigger.mute:w:0\ntrigger.unmute:w:1' ]] || fail "menu offers Unmute and not Mute while the output is muted"
pass "menu offers Unmute and not Mute while the output is muted"
```

## Actual output

At the reviewed head (6d7c9ab8), exit 0:

```
ok - mute sets output to muted and shows the OSD
ok - mute does not unmute an already muted output
ok - unmute sets output to unmuted and shows the OSD
ok - unmute does not mute an already unmuted output
ok - menu offers Mute and not Unmute while the output is unmuted
ok - menu offers Unmute and not Mute while the output is muted
```

With M1 or M2 applied, exit 1 (stdout shows the four existing `ok` lines, stderr):

```
not ok - menu offers Mute and not Unmute while the output is unmuted
```
</details>

# Related open PR #13405: combination notes for `bin/omarchy-audio-output-volume`

Status: merge-order heads-up for whichever of #13494 / #13405 lands second. Neither PR is wrong on its own.

Pinned heads: #13494 6d7c9ab8, #13405 d6e303b7.

## 1. Textual conflict (metadata header only)

A three-way merge of the two heads conflicts only in the header, lines 3-5:

```
<<<<<<< #13494
# omarchy:summary=Adjust output volume and show the Omarchy OSD
# omarchy:args=<raise|lower|mute|unmute|mute-toggle|+N|-N>
# omarchy:examples=omarchy audio output volume raise | omarchy audio output volume mute | omarchy audio output volume unmute | omarchy audio output volume mute-toggle | omarchy audio output volume +1
=======
# omarchy:summary=Adjust output volume and show the Omarchy OSD. Drives the hardware mute LED on laptops that expose one.
# omarchy:args=<raise|lower|mute-toggle|+N|-N>
# omarchy:examples=omarchy audio output volume raise | omarchy audio output volume lower | omarchy audio output volume mute-toggle | omarchy audio output volume +1
>>>>>>> #13405
```

Resolution: keep #13405's summary line and #13494's args/examples lines. The body merges cleanly, and #13405's LED block sits after the whole action chain, so it also runs after `mute` and `unmute`.

## 2. Once combined, this PR's test calls an unstubbed helper

`test/shell.d/audio-output-volume-test.sh` stubs `omarchy-audio-output-sink`, `pactl` and `omarchy-osd`, then prepends its stub directory to the inherited `PATH`. With #13405's block in the script, each of the test's volume runs also calls `omarchy-brightness-keyboard-mute on|off platform::mute`, which the test does not stub. It therefore resolves to whatever copy is on the developer's `PATH`.

Reproduce (combined tree, a logging stand-in for the helper first on `PATH`):

```bash
git fetch origin pull/13494/head:pr-13494 pull/13405/head:pr-13405
git checkout pr-13494
git merge --no-edit pr-13405        # resolve the header as above, then commit
helper_dir=$(mktemp -d)
cat >"$helper_dir/omarchy-brightness-keyboard-mute" <<'SH'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"${0%/*}/calls"
SH
chmod +x "$helper_dir/omarchy-brightness-keyboard-mute"
PATH="$helper_dir:$PATH" bash test/shell.d/audio-output-volume-test.sh
cat "$helper_dir/calls"
```

The run below used `git merge-file` with the same merge base (which produced the identical header conflict) instead of the `git merge` line, then the resolution above; the logging stand-in and the test invocation were equivalent to the ones shown. Actual output (exit 0):

```
ok - mute sets output to muted and shows the OSD
ok - mute does not unmute an already muted output
ok - unmute sets output to unmuted and shows the OSD
ok - unmute does not mute an already unmuted output
```

and the helper log:

```
on platform::mute
on platform::mute
off platform::mute
off platform::mute
```

What an installed helper would do there is read from source, not executed: #13405's `omarchy-brightness-keyboard-mute` runs `brightnessctl --device=platform::mute set 1|0` when `/sys/class/leds/platform::mute/brightness` exists (and the current helper ignores the second argument and drives `platform::micmute`). So on a laptop with that LED, running the test would switch the real indicator and leave it off.

Suggested change for whichever PR lands second: stub the helper in the test, after the existing stubs and before the first volume run, for example:

```bash
cat >"$stub_dir/omarchy-brightness-keyboard-mute" <<'STUB'
#!/bin/bash
printf '%s\n' "$*" >>"$AUDIO_TEST_DIR/led"
STUB
chmod +x "$stub_dir/omarchy-brightness-keyboard-mute"
```
</details>
